description: Solo team LunaSolo from Harohalli. Building Earth System Trend Detection for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Analyzing 24 years of NASA / NOAA climate data (2000-2024) to detect trends in temperature, CO2, Arctic ice and sea level, and forecast to 2030 using Python.
summary: LunaSolo - Earth System Trend Detection tracks how our planet changed from 2000 to 2024. I analysed 4 real signals from NASA, NOAA, and NSIDC: global temperature, CO2, Arctic sea ice, and sea level. Using Python, Pandas, and Linear Regression in Google Colab, I cleaned the data, found long-term trends, and forecasted to 2030. Temperature rose by 0.9°C and is predicted to reach 1.23°C by 2030. CO2 is predicted to reach 434.2 ppm. Arctic ice fell by 30% and sea level rose by 80mm. My project makes complex climate data simple and visual, so anyone can see that all 4 signals agree - Earth is warming fast. It helps students, citizens, and decision-makers understand why urgent action is needed.
details: LunaSolo is a data analysis dashboard that detects trends in Earth's system from 2000-2024. I collected open data from NASA GISS for temperature, NOAA for CO2 and sea level, and NSIDC for Arctic sea ice. I used Python, Pandas for cleaning, Matplotlib for graphs, and Linear Regression for forecasting to 2030 in Google Colab. The tool shows 4 clear trends in one place, instead of searching 4 different websites. Its benefit is simple, evidence-based climate education. Its impact is to help people trust real data, not rumours. My creative idea was "One Planet, Four Signals" - showing that all signals point to the same warming story. I considered data accuracy, simple visuals, and honest forecasting without exaggeration. All data, analysis, graphs, and forecasts were done by me using real data. AI was used only to help improve the wording of titles and the summary.
